stem: During a non-urgent lumbar puncture, what is the main drawback of injecting local anaesthetic before identifying landmarks?

options.text: It removes the need for a sterile drape
It means the needle must be inserted above L3/L4
It removes the need to aim towards the umbilicus

explanation: It can obscure landmarks. Local anaesthetic may be used for comfort, but injecting it before landmark identification can make palpation and accurate site selection harder during a lumbar puncture.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Local anaesthetic injection may obscure lumbar puncture landmarks.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because injecting local anaesthetic before landmark identification can obscure the bony landmarks needed to guide a lumbar puncture.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because side positioning can still be used for a lumbar puncture; local anaesthetic does not make that position unsuitable.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because sterile preparation is still required, including skin cleaning and a sterile drape.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the insertion level remains between L3/L4 or L4/L5; local anaesthetic does not change the recommended level.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the needle is still directed towards the umbilicus; local anaesthetic does not alter that technique.
